human_summary: Independent print-only inspection of four pages and twenty systems confirms 94 printed physical regions and the proposed frame. All crop boundaries retain the essential musical ink. Pickups, partial bars, four changes of key, section double barlines and the final barline were checked directly. All systems use treble clef above and bass clef below; no clef changes are printed. No repeats, endings, route marks or bars split across systems are printed. Geometry assistance contains duplicate stroke candidates and four false staff-end candidates after cautionary signatures; these do not change the proposed lock. Only the authorized request, hashed print inputs and proposed print-only frame/geometry inputs were used; no reader outputs, candidate transcription, repair findings or prior verifier verdicts were accessed.

irregular_checks.question_plain: How do the short regions around the key change divide the metre?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: P057 contains a dotted half tied to a quarter and then a sixteenth on both staves: eight eighth-note units and one sixteenth-note unit. P058 is one sixteenth-note unit, completing nine eighth-note units together. The final flagged note is separate from the continuous closing double barline.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Is the key-signature area an additional region?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. A complete double barline closes P018 at crop x 1517. The cancellation and three sharps are cautionary; the remaining staff lines reach the system edge without an additional barline. P018 itself is a dotted half plus dotted quarter, a complete nine-eight bar.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does the final region close completely?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. Dotted half and dotted quarter total nine eighth-note units. The thin and thick closing strokes form one final boundary, fully inside the crop.

irregular_checks.where: All four pages and all twenty systems
irregular_checks.question_plain: Are there later clef or metre changes, repeats, endings, route marks or bars split at system breaks?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. Each system prints treble clef above and bass clef below, without any mid-system or cautionary clef changes. Nine-eight remains in force. There are no repeat dots, ending brackets or route instructions. Every system has a closing barline; ties and slurs crossing a system break do not split a physical bar.

count_anomaly_review.explanation_plain: Independent region counts in system order 1 through 20: 5, 4, 5, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 5, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5, 5, 6, 4, 4, 4, totaling 94. Counted each space between successive continuous grand-staff boundaries once. Paired thin strokes at section changes and thin/thick final strokes are single boundaries. Closely adjacent geometry detections are the same ink, not extra bars. Systems 4, 8, 12 and 16 continue staff lines after a closing double barline to carry a cautionary key signature; those staff ends contain no extra vertical barline and add no regions. Note stems stop within a staff or terminate at their noteheads/beams; they do not trace through both staves and the connecting space. All system-end barlines are present, including at ties and slurs continued on the next system. Pickups and partials remain distinct printed regions.
